articles.title: JP Morgan Strategist on AI Jitters, Investing Outlook
articles.summary: Jordan Jackson, JPMorgan Asset Management Global Market Strategist, discusses whether earnings growth may be nearing a peak even if results are not worsening. Jackson agrees that third-quarter results are expected to be strong, with forecasts calling for about 27% to 28% year-over-year earnings growth. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Kristine Aquino on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Financing The AI Boom: Masters in Business with Bob Michele
articles.summary: Barry speaks with Bob Michele, CIO and Head of Global Fixed Income, Currency, and Commodities at JPMorgan. They discuss Bob's unconventional start at the University of Pennsylvania, the differences between the science of bonds and the art of equities, and whether the US is heading toward a recession. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: SoftBank Is Said to Weigh Buying Top US Security Firm Allied
articles.summary: SoftBank Group Corp. is considering an acquisition of Allied Universal, the largest security services company in the US, people familiar with the matter said, as founder Masayoshi Son explores ways to deploy AI-powered robots across industries.
articles.author: Carmen Arroyo, Min Jeong Lee, Manuel Baigorri and Paula Sambo

articles.title: CoreWeave, Nscale Put Neocloud Economics in Focus
articles.summary: Concerns about the enormous amounts of debt financing the AI infrastructure boom are putting the neocloud sector under increasing scrutiny. Decoding Discontinuity CEO Raphaelle D’Ornano discusses the pressure on CoreWeave as interest expenses weigh on its economics. She explains why investors are looking beyond contracted backlogs to financed and energized capacity, and how Nscale’s vertically integrated approach differs as it prepares for a potential IPO. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Nscale's Flagship Data Center Hit by Delays Ahead of IPO
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence infrastructure firm Nscale is seeking to raise up to $3 billion in an initial public offering as soon as this month, just as investors are growing increasingly wary of the risks of the AI buildout. The UK firm has also been hit by regulatory hurdles, a fire and other delays during construction of a flagship data center in Norway. Bloomberg's Paula Doenecke reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Startup‑time budget for React Native apps using Hermes
articles.summary: The situation Say you are a lead mobile engineer at a two‑year‑old fintech startup. The product ships daily to both iOS and Android, and the next release is due in two weeks. The product manager has just received a user‑experience survey that shows a 30 % drop‑off on the first screen for Android users who open the app from a cold state. The crash‑free rate is unchanged, but the analytics dashboard reports that the average cold‑start time has risen from 1.8 s to 2.4 s on the most common Android handset (Pixel 5, Android 13). Your team has already enabled Hermes 0.13.1 in the Android Gradle file, but the metric is still above the target. The product manager has asked for “faster startup” and threatens to postpone the feature release unless you can prove that the app will launch under 1.5 s on the same device. The cost of missing the deadline is concrete: a delayed feature rollout, a potential loss of $150 k in projected revenue, and a week of overtime for the mobile squad. Why it happens

articles.title: React Frontend Plus NodeJS Backend Error Capture for Tenant Cohort Incident Reconstruction
articles.summary: A thin correlation layer beats a large monitoring rollout when the immediate job is reconstructing which tenant cohort saw a fintech experiment fail. TL;DR: generate a trace_id at the browser boundary, forward it through the API, and put it on both backend logs and sanitized frontend error reports. Use a dedicated browser product when source maps or replay decide the investigation; use a tracing product when engineers need a span tree rather than manual correlation. articles.title: Stocks Rotate as Tech & Chip Shares Slide

articles.title: Don't See Canary in Coal Mine For AI: Khoda
articles.summary: Neha Khoda, head of US credit strategy at BofA Securities, and Stephanie Doyle, fixed income portfolio manager at JPMorgan Investment Management, join Scarlet Fu on "Bloomberg Real Yield." A measure of CoreWeave’s credit risk climbed to an all-time high Thursday as some of its high-yield bonds extended declines, rattled by the AI cloud-computing company’s talk of tapping vast pools of capital from insurers. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Anthropic Stands Alone as Rest of US IPO Market Slows to a Crawl
articles.summary: A cocktail of risks is threatening to stall the US IPO pipeline, leaving Anthropic PBC’s potential blockbuster debut as one of the few offerings that investors can count on.
articles.author: Anthony Hughes and Bailey Lipschultz

articles.title: Anthropic’s IPO Momentum as CoreWeave Rattles AI Trade
articles.summary: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow breaks down Anthropic's third-quarter revenue numbers as the company gets ready for its IPO. Plus: CoreWeave’s talk of tapping “unlimited” pools of money rattles markets and puts the financing behind the data center buildout back under the microscope; and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says safety and containment should be integrated into AI systems even as AI advances. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Inside Blackstone’s Massive Bet on the AI Boom
articles.summary: Blackstone has built one of Wall Street’s broadest bets on AI, investing across the ecosystem from data centers, power and cooling to chip financing and companies including OpenAI, Anthropic and SpaceX. Bloomberg’s Preeti Singh explains how President and COO Jon Gray spotted the infrastructure opportunity early and why he sees AI as a generational economic shift that investors can’t afford to ignore. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Anthropic's Q3 revenue hits $16.8B but growth slows ahead of planned November IPO
articles.summary: Anthropic hit $16.8 billion in third-quarter revenue, a 45 percent gain that still falls far short of Q2's 140 percent surge. With a November IPO approaching, some investors now expect the company's valuation to drop below $1.5 trillion. Slowing growth and a tough market are cooling expectations for the AI boom's biggest Wall Street test yet. The article Anthropic's Q3 revenue hits $16.8B but growth slows ahead of planned November IPO appeared first on The Decoder.
articles.author: Matthias Bastian

articles.title: Anthropic Urged to Pause IPO for AI Safety by NYC Comptroller
articles.summary: Anthropic should pause its initial public offering until it has fully addressed risks around artificial intelligence, according to New York City’s comptroller. A letter from Mark Levine addressed to Anthropic Chief Executive Officer Dario Amodei on Wednesday suggested the Claude developer should instead focus on addressing the unprecedented risks of the technology. Ed Ludlow reports on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Santander's Ana Botin on US Growth, Debt, AI and the Global Economy | The David Rubenstein Show
articles.summary: Santander Executive Chair Ana Botin sits down with David Rubenstein to discuss the bank's expansion in the US, including its recent acquisition of Webster Financial, and why she sees lack of economic growth as one of the biggest challenges facing the global economy. She also discusses US debt, the outlook for the US and European economies amid geopolitical uncertainty, and the impact of AI on banking and jobs. Botin is on this week's episode of The David Rubenstein Show: Peer to Peer Conversations. This episode was recorded July 13 in New York. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Ramp Completes Funding at $60 Billion Value as Revenue Surges
articles.summary: Ramp has surged to $2 billion in annualized revenue, the fintech company plans to announce Thursday — a milestone that’s helped attract fresh investor capital.

articles.title: SmartNews Said to Plan December Tokyo IPO as Valuation Craters
articles.summary: SmartNews Inc. is planning an initial public offering in December at a fraction of its previous valuation, according to people familiar with the matter, a sign of the news aggregator’s business being decimated by artificial intelligence.

articles.title: Accumulating Empty Video Rooms: Cleanup by Lease Generation and Reconciliation
articles.summary: Do not destroy a video room on the last leave event. Mark it empty, wait through a bounded grace period, and then require a second, authoritative occupancy check before teardown. For a fintech support call that also exposes typing indicators and read receipts, this rule keeps presence accurate during reconnects while ensuring abandoned sessions cannot accumulate forever. TL;DR: Treat room deletion as a state transition, not an event callback. A leave signal starts suspicion; a later observation proves absence. Make teardown idempotent, retain a periodic reconciler as the repair path, and measure how long rooms remain empty rather than counting successful callbacks. That distinction matters because WebRTC describes peer connections, not the application-level membership of a room. The W3C API exposes connection state and a way to close an RTCPeerConnection, but it does not appoint the browser, signaling node, or media layer as the owner of a shared room record. articles.title: Nvidia, Anthropic Weigh In On AI Safeguards
articles.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said he would halt the supply of chips to a customer that was developing unsafe AI software, though he doesn’t believe that the current level of concern about the technology is warranted. AI executives such as Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei have proposed an industrywide slowdown to address the concerns. Meantime, Anthropic held an investor day Wednesday as it advances plans for a potential IPO at an approximately $2 trillion valuation, amid growing concerns about AI safety and threats. We get reaction from Bloomberg Tech host Ed Ludlow & Jacqueline Corbelli, Co-Founder and CEO at Brightline Partners. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Inflation Rises as Fuel Costs Surge
articles.summary: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Vonnie Quinn on "Bloomberg Open Interest." Inflation heats up as fuel prices risev and Middle East tensions threaten more pressure ahead. Big bank earnings expose a divide on Wall Street. RBC’s Gerard Cassidy breaks down rates, margins and credit risk. Plus, AI demand keeps surging. Stripe Vice Chair Eileen O’Mara on Europe’s startup push and how agentic commerce could transform payments. (Source: Bloomberg)
